newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts lose.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts lose.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended mixed Tuesday in a moderate session, with front months pressured by a stalled rally in the cash and some technical selling after four straight gains, traders said.
October slipped 3.9 cents to close at $1.934 per million British thermal units. November settled 1.6 cents lower at $2.151. Other deferreds ended mixed.

"I expected some profit taking after four straight up days, but there's still a lot of demand for storage," said one Houston-based trader, adding October's failure this morning to break the $2 resistance mark triggered technical selling.
Despite forecasts for more mild weather next week, some expected steady storage buying to continue to prop up physical prices near-term.
"There's still a need to get gas in the ground in the producing region and that could give some support to the market," said one trader.
Technically, some traders said the market may be range-bound, with October support at the $1.88-1.885 gap and psychological resistance at $2.

While cash prices finished up slightly by nomination deadlines, traders noted a sharp early rally was stalled by good selling. Gulf Coast prices were steady to up a couple of cents to the $1.85-1.90 area. Midcon pipes gained more than five cents to the mid-$1.70s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip edged up 0.2 cent to $2.084. NYMEX said 38,104 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 35,801.
NYMEX October Permian natgas closed one cent higher at $1.65, while deferreds were untraded and settled unchanged. NYMEX said 41 Permian contracts traded versus 16 on Monday.

On the KCBT, October finished three cents lower at $1.72, while deferreds ended steady to down one-half cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.9 cent to 21.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 244 lots traded, down from Monday's total of 286.
